column3: Biallelic BUB1B variants pair a null or truncating allele with a hypomorphic missense or regulatory allele, so cells carry a reduced but non-zero amount of BubR1. Below a threshold, the residual protein can neither sustain the mitotic checkpoint complex that restrains APC/C-Cdc20 nor recruit PP2A-B56 to kinetochores to stabilise microtubule attachments. Anaphase begins before chromosomes are correctly attached, chromatids separate prematurely, and each division adds new aneuploid cells, which is why the aneuploidy is mosaic and variegated rather than uniform. Aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and metabolic stress and are arrested, senesced or cleared, which is proposed to deplete progenitor pools and produce growth restriction and microcephaly, while the surviving aneuploid clones carry an elevated risk of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour and leukaemia. The quantity that is deficient is BubR1 protein, and that is where a therapy has to act.
column7: Growth restriction and microcephaly in this disorder are established in utero and are structural at birth. No post-natal increase in BubR1 abundance can reverse them, so a mechanistically correct agent can still be therapeutically irrelevant to the features that are most visible. What post-natal correction could plausibly change is the rate at which NEW aneuploid cells are generated from that point on, and therefore the trajectory of cancer risk and of progeroid tissue attrition. Any claim of benefit must state which of those it means, and the trial endpoint has to match: a cytogenetic or tumour-incidence endpoint is arguable, a head-circumference endpoint is not.
